scenes.title: Integrate and extend the What-If Tool
scenes.subtitle: APIs, JSON, the database and the AI layer
scenes.narration: A developer's tour of the What-If Tool: its API, the JSON in and out, the database, the AI layer, and how to extend it.

scenes.caption: Two flows: data in, people out
scenes.narration: Two flows. Your systems post JSON to the backend API, which validates it, computes what it can, and stores it in PostgreSQL. The browser runs the React app: it reads results over REST, and calls the language model itself, through an nginx proxy, to Ollama on the host. The backend never calls a model.

scenes.caption: Live docs at /swagger
scenes.narration: Every endpoint is documented live at slash swagger: three domains, education, yard logistics and check-in logs, with schemas from the code and a curl for every call. There's no authentication yet, so put it behind your own gateway.

scenes.title: Send simulator runs as they are
scenes.note: The export is stored verbatim. Add later runs with POST /:caseId/runs.
scenes.narration: Yard data goes in exactly as the simulator wrote it. You add a case name, and per run an id and a label; the export is stored as is. Later runs go to the case's runs endpoint, a natural webhook target.

scenes.title: Errors that tell you what to fix
scenes.note: 400 means understood but rejected. 422 means the body broke its schema.

highlights.label: a fix, not just a fail

scenes.narration: The backend checks only the four parts it reads, and rejects anything else with a 400 that says what's wrong. A body that breaks the schema gets a 422.

scenes.title: A what-if is a list of typed adjustments
scenes.note: Nine types, applied in a fixed order. Week indexes start at zero.
scenes.narration: For education, a what-if is a named list of typed adjustments, posted to a case's scenarios endpoint. They apply in a fixed order: assignment and exam changes, a schedule rebuild, then lecture, lab and homework changes.

scenes.title: Every result carries its own audit trail
scenes.note: A 201 means it ran, not that it helped.
scenes.narration: Every result is an audit trail. Here every adjustment applied, but the peak still rose, so improved is false. A two-oh-one means it ran, not that it helped: check improved, and each adjustment's status and code.

scenes.title: Raw JSON kept, metrics computed once
points: Partner JSON stored as JSONB, exactly as sent
Yard metrics and log aggregates computed at ingest
Timelines and sessions rebuilt per request
Schema change: schema.sql + schema.ts + a migration
scenes.narration: In PostgreSQL, partner data is stored as JSON B exactly as sent, so new fields never need a migration. Derived numbers are computed once at ingest; cheap views are rebuilt per request. Schema changes go in the SQL file, the Drizzle schema, and a migration.

scenes.caption: The AI layer lives in the browser
scenes.narration: Every model call comes from the browser: a feature calls a React hook, which calls one file, ollama service dot T S, then an nginx proxy, then Ollama on the host.

scenes.title: One request per chat message
scenes.note: The system message is rebuilt from page data every time. Nothing is stored server-side.
scenes.narration: Here's the logs chat request: model, streaming, a low temperature, a reply cap, and messages. The system message is rebuilt from page data every time; nothing is stored server-side.

scenes.title: Three ways to swap the model
points: Any Ollama model: pull it, pick it. No code
An Ollama-compatible server: point the proxy at it
OpenAI-style or hosted APIs: rewrite ollamaService.ts
API keys never in VITE_ variables: server-side, auth first
scenes.narration: Three ways to swap the model. Any Ollama model: pull it and pick it. An Ollama-compatible server: point the proxy at it. OpenAI-style or hosted APIs: write an adapter in ollama service dot T S. And never put an API key in a VITE variable; keep it server-side, behind authentication.

scenes.title: Three recipes you will reach for
points: A new use case: copy the logs domain, end to end
A new adjustment type: adjustments.ts and simulate.ts
A new proposal change: type, validation and the prompt
Every change: example bodies, spec and tests
scenes.narration: Three recipes cover most extensions. A new use case: copy the logs domain end to end. A new adjustment type: adjustments and simulate. A new proposal change: its type, validation, and the prompt's schema, or the parser drops it.

scenes.title: Hook points and gotchas
points: Example bodies double as test fixtures
No auth, open CORS: lock both down
Send to simulator: specified, not built yet
scenes.narration: To integrate, push each finished run to the runs endpoint and read results with plain gets; the example bodies double as test fixtures. Watch out: Ollama must allow the app's origin, there's no authentication and CORS is open, and sending proposals to the simulator isn't built yet.

scenes.title: Build on it
scenes.subtitle: Every endpoint, contract and recipe: the developer guide.
scenes.narration: Every endpoint, contract and recipe is in the developer guide. Thanks for watching.
